description.to:
Outcome: Later option (owner decision D): a tenant admin enters its own Google OAuth client id and secret; the platform signs that tenant's people in through it. Design, subject to PPY-8eca5b: storage in SSM Parameter Store SecureString under a tenant-scoped path, /papyrus/shared/tenants/<tenant>/google-oauth/client-id and /client-secret (owner rule: SSM over Secrets Manager); written only by a 'set sign-in client' function called by a tenant admin claim (the secret is write-only: never returned by the API or logged); validation before use: format checks, the redirect URI we show must be registered in the tenant's Google project, and the new client starts 'pending' until the admin completes one test sign-in through it; then the function creates or updates the tenant's OIDC provider in the pool (and its app client if the spike shows one is needed), and the newsroom offers it for that site. Rotation: the admin submits a new secret, a new parameter version is written, the provider is updated, the test sign-in repeats, the old version is kept until it passes. Removal or failure: the provider is detached and the tenant falls back to the shared Google client the same minute; members keep access because membership is keyed on the UserProfile (mapped from both subs through UserIdentity), not on one provider's sub. Every change is audited (PPY-1da916).

Touches (verified at origin/develop 23fabe1d): new amplify/functions/tenant-signin-client/, SSM paths under /papyrus/shared/tenants/, amplify/auth (pool-level IAM for UpdateIdentityProvider / CreateIdentityProvider), TenantMembership keyed by userProfileId, UserIdentity, app/newsroom sign-in settings.

Acceptance (Gherkin feature file: features_backend/tenant-own-google-client.feature):
Scenario: A tenant's own client is used only after a test sign-in
    Given alpha's admin enters a client id and secret
    When she completes a test sign-in through it
    Then alpha's members sign in through alpha's client and the secret was never shown again

Scenario: Removing the client falls back to the shared one
    Given alpha uses its own client
    When the admin removes it
    Then alpha's members sign in with the shared Google client and keep their roles

Dependencies: blocked by PPY-8eca5b, PPY-fdbbd7, PPY-1da916. Blocks nothing in this plan yet. (Also recorded as kbs dependencies.)
Implements or extends: -.

Testing: Behave in a sandbox pool; adversarial cases: a tenant admin cannot set or read another tenant's client.
Rollout: After M7 (not needed for launch).
Risk and mitigation: Risk: a broken tenant client locks its members out. Mitigation: pending state plus test sign-in, automatic fallback to the shared client on provider errors, operator reset.

Releasable on its own: yes.
DynamoDB index: none.
AppSync authorisation: changes: tenant admins can change their tenant's sign-in provider.
Design note: docs/plans/multi-tenant-architecture.md (PR on branch docs/multi-tenant-architecture).
